cor.heading: Cost of Revenue
cor.text:
Cost of revenue primarily includes raw materials for product manufacturing, shipping and handling costs, third-party costs for outsourced products and services, payroll and related expenses, information technology costs, depreciation and amortization of production and digital assets, residuals paid to independent sales organizations (ISOs), and related overhead.

Total cost of revenue increased in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025. The increases were primarily driven by higher costs associated with growth in our payments and data businesses, including the impact of the Celero acquisition, lower vendor rebates in our data-driven marketing business compared to the prior year, and inflationary pressures on materials and delivery costs.

These increases were partially offset by lower costs associated with soft demand for promotional products and the continued secular declines in the Print segment, as well as the impact of our cost management initiatives.

opex.text: SG&A expense increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by costs associated with the Celero acquisition, including transaction costs of $9.8 million, amortization expense of $10.9 million, and the ongoing operating expenses of the acquired business. Partially offsetting these increases was the first quarter business exit discussed in the Executive Overview section, which reduced SG&A expense by approximately $16.8 million in the third quarter of 2026. SG&A expense also benefited from our ongoing cost management initiatives, including workforce adjustments across multiple functions, and lower commission expense driven by lower Print revenue volumes.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expense
sga.text:
SG&A expense increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by costs associated with the Celero acquisition, including transaction costs of $9.8 million, amortization expense of $10.9 million, and the ongoing operating expenses of the acquired business. Partially offsetting these increases was the first quarter business exit discussed in the Executive Overview section, which reduced SG&A expense by approximately $16.8 million in the third quarter of 2026. SG&A expense also benefited from our ongoing cost management initiatives, including workforce adjustments across multiple functions, and lower commission expense driven by lower Print revenue volumes.

As a percentage of total revenue, SG&A expense increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, as the impact of transaction costs and amortization expense associated with the Celero acquisition more than offset our cost management actions and the impact of the first quarter business exit.

SG&A expense decreased in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the first nine months of 2025, primarily driven by the first quarter business exit discussed in the Executive Overview section, which reduced SG&A expense by approximately $39.7 million.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to higher average debt outstanding as a result of the financing of the Celero acquisition. This increase was partially offset by a lower weighted-average interest rate.

Interest expense decreased in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the first nine months of 2025, primarily due to a lower weighted-average interest rate. This decrease was partially offset by higher average debt outstanding as a result of the financing of the Celero acquisition.

As of September 30, 2026, $500.5 million of our debt was subject to variable rates, after giving effect to our interest rate swaps. Changes in market interest rates on this debt could affect our interest expense. Based on the amount of variable-rate debt outstanding as of September 30, 2026, a one percentage point change in the weighted-average interest rate would result in a $1.3 million impact on interest expense for the remainder of 2026.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
Total revenue increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by growth in our Merchant Services segment, including the impact of the Celero acquisition on July 31, 2026, which contributed revenue of $33.5 million. Strong demand for our data-driven marketing services also contributed to the increase, resulting in $13.9 million of additional revenue compared to the prior-year quarter. Revenue growth was further supported by strategic price increases implemented in response to inflationary pressures, particularly within our Merchant Services and Print segments.

These favorable factors were partially offset by the first quarter business exit discussed in the Executive Overview section, which reduced revenue by approximately $32.3 million. Soft demand for promotional products and the continued secular decline in order volumes for checks, business forms, and business accessories within our Print segment also negatively impacted revenue.

Total revenue decreased in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the first nine months of 2025, primarily due to the first quarter business exit discussed in the Executive Overview section, which reduced revenue by approximately $79.3 million.

Checks.text: Total revenue decreased in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025, primarily driven by weaker demand for promotional products and the ongoing secular decline in order volumes for checks, business forms, and various business accessories. In addition, the sale of the Safeguard small business distributor channel in the first quarter of 2026 reduced revenue by approximately $32.3 million in the third quarter and $79.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 . These declines were partially offset by pricing actions implemented to address inflationary pressures.

Data-driven marketing.text: These unfavorable factors were partially offset by strong demand for our data-driven marketing services, which contributed $49.0 million of additional revenue compared to the prior-year period. Revenue also benefited from growth in our Merchant Services segment, including $33.5 million of revenue from the Celero acquisition, as well as strategic price increases, particularly within our Merchant Services and Print segments. Growth in our B2B segment, driven by new lockbox and remittance processing clients and a software license agreement within our broader suite of treasury management offerings, also contributed to revenue.

Service.heading: Merchant Services
Service.text:
Results for our Merchant Services segment were as follows:

Total revenue increased in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025, driven by revenue from the Celero acquisition, new customer implementations, higher transaction volumes from existing partners across several channels, and targeted pricing actions. The Celero acquisition, which closed on July 31, 2026, contributed $33.5 million of revenue in both periods. These increases were partially offset by pressure on consumer and business spending in certain customer channels.

Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin also improved in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025, reflecting contributions from the Celero acquisition and new customer implementations, targeted pricing actions, and cost management initiatives. These initiatives included the purchase of residual commission rights from an ISO partner in late 2025, which reduced ongoing commission expense.

intro.text: Deluxe, a trusted Payments and Data company, champions business so communities thrive. Our solutions help businesses pay, get paid, and grow. For more than 100 years, Deluxe customers have relied on our solutions and platforms at all stages of their lifecycle, from start-up to maturity. Our powerful scale supports millions of small businesses, thousands of vital financial institutions, and hundreds of the world’s largest consumer brands, while processing more than $2 trillion in annual payment volume. Our reach, scale, and distribution channels position Deluxe to be our customers’ most trusted business partner. To learn how we can help your business, visit us at www.deluxe.com , www.facebook.com/deluxecorp , www.linkedin.com/company/deluxe , or www.x.com/deluxe .

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
